rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §17 hides the whole span walk (extended from h2 to every level, with identity, level, text, span, landed-card flag and enclosing element) behind one public `plan_headings` reader over one private read, and §16 folds tag-stripping, entity decoding and skip-tag removal behind `strip_tags`; the complexity stays in the private parser, not spread over wrappers.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: pass — §17 hoists `section_record_id`/`section_id_candidates`/`section_anchor` out of `reckon/crew/routing.py` into `reckon/_plan_html.py` (the core owner) and repoints every importer including promotion's module-level import (`reckon/crew/promotion.py:77`), moves `landed_section_ids` from `_store.py` to its one home, and converges the `data-reckon` marker (14 lines/5 files), the `section-landed` class (5 lines) and the section-spelling grammars onto single exported owners rather than forking them.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1478, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §16 and §17 add only to public_definitions and each states in its own text why nothing can be retired (the two public readers keep cross-module callers; the identity digest and prose walk keep their names), §16 explicitly reuses the existing plan-review-missing refusal family rather than adding one, and neither section adds a CLI option or MCP view.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan searched the codebase and every base census it cites checks out against the live tree: `_StructuredSectionSpanParser`/`structured_section_spans` in `reckon/_plan_html.py`, `_TAG_RE`/`count_open_decisions` (same file), `landed_section_ids` (`reckon/_store.py:1075`), `section_record_id`/`section_id_candidates`/`section_anchor` (`reckon/crew/routing.py:224,243,238`), `_PROSE_SKIP_TAGS`/`_AuthoredProseParser` (`reckon/crew/plan_review.py:147,168`), and the `interface_counts.py` AST census are all real and named as the mechanisms to extend.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — both new public faces state why the existing machinery cannot be extended in place: §16 exposes the existing `_TAG_RE` expression across the package boundary rather than adding a second one beside it (its consumer in `reckon/crew` crosses the boundary), and §17 keeps the parser private and projects its output through two public views rather than adding a scanner.
